chunks: Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari narrated from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, who said:

I asked Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad عليه السلام about two groups among the believers, one of them rebellious and the other just, who fought one another. Then a man from the people of Iraq killed his father, or his son, or his brother, or his close relative, while he was from the people of rebellion and was his heir. I asked: “Does he inherit from him?” He said: “Yes, because he killed him rightfully.”

key_terms.بَاغِيَةٌ: rebellious; a faction acting in wrongful revolt
key_terms.طَائِفَتَيْنِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: two groups from among the believers

ai.seo_question: Does a person still inherit if he killed his relative lawfully in battle against a rebellious group?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on inheritance in the context of fighting between a rebellious faction and a just faction among the believers. It states that if an heir kills his relative in a lawful act of fighting against the people of rebellion, that killing does not prevent him from inheriting.
